user.description: Choose an iPixel LED matrix that Home Assistant can currently see over Bluetooth.

data_description.height: Height of the matrix in pixels. Text is drawn at 16 or 32 pixels high.
data_description.width: Width of the matrix in pixels. Pictures are resized to this.

abort.no_devices_found: No iPixel matrices (named LED_BLE_…) are in Bluetooth range.
abort.not_supported: This Bluetooth device is not an iPixel matrix.

init.title: Message defaults
init.description: Used when the Message entity is set. The display_text action can override each one.

data_description.width: Width of the matrix in pixels. Pictures are resized to this.
data_description.connect_via: Bluetooth adapter or ESPHome Bluetooth proxy to reach the matrix through. Automatic uses whichever has the best signal.
data_description.keep_connected: Keep the Bluetooth connection open between sends, so the matrix does not show its connecting icon each time and updates start sooner. While connected, the phone app cannot reach the matrix.
data_description.idle_disconnect: Minutes with nothing sent before a kept connection is closed, freeing the matrix for the phone app. 0 never disconnects.
data_description.font_path: Optional full path to a .ttf or .otf file, for example /config/fonts/MyFont.ttf. Leave empty for the built-in font.
data_description.effect: How the text moves on the matrix.
data_description.rainbow_mode: 0 or 1 shows the text in its solid colour; 2 to 9 are rainbow presets.
data_description.save_slot: Program slot on the matrix that the message is stored in.

error.invalid_font: The font file could not be loaded.

display_text.name: Display text
display_text.description: Shows a message on the LED matrix.

message.name: Message
message.description: Text to show. Line breaks become spaces.

color.name: Text colour
color.description: Colour of the text. Defaults to the colour in the integration's options.

background_color.name: Background colour
background_color.description: Background colour. Leave empty for no background.

effect.name: Animation
effect.description: How the text moves. Defaults to the animation in the integration's options (scroll left unless changed).

rainbow_mode.name: Rainbow mode
rainbow_mode.description: 0 or 1 shows the text in its solid colour; 2 to 9 are rainbow presets.

save_slot.name: Save slot
save_slot.description: Program slot on the matrix that the message is stored in (1 to 10).

display_image.name: Display image
display_image.description: Shows a picture or animated GIF on the LED matrix, resized to fit it.

file.name: File
file.description: Path of a picture on the Home Assistant host, in /config/www or another allowed folder. PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF and WebP work. Give a file or a URL.

url.name: URL
url.description: Web address of a picture to download. Give a file or a URL.

resize.name: Resize
resize.description: How the picture is fitted to the panel. Defaults to Fit.

background_color.name: Background colour
background_color.description: Colour for transparent areas and for the padding in Fit mode. Defaults to black.

save_slot.name: Save slot
save_slot.description: Program slot on the matrix that the picture is stored in (1 to 10).

hide_loading.name: Hide loading
hide_loading.description: Set the panel's brightness to 0 while the picture is sent, then put it back, so the panel's own loading animation is not seen.

live.name: Live
live.description: Show the picture straight away as a live frame instead of saving it in a slot (like the app's camera mode). Only the first frame of an animation is shown, and save slot and hide loading are not used.

display_graph.name: Display graph
display_graph.description: Draws a list of numbers as a bar graph, or x-y points as a line or dot graph, scaled to fill the LED matrix.

values.name: Values
values.description: Numbers to plot evenly spaced, oldest on the left, for example [0, 2, 5, 7]. Up to 1024. As bars, negative values count as 0. Give only one of values, points and series.

points.name: Points
points.description: x-y pairs to plot, for example [[0, 1.2], [15, 3.4], [60, 2.0]]. Up to 1024.

series.name: Series
series.description: Several sets of points, up to 8, each a mapping with points and an optional color, for example [{"points": [[0, 1], [60, 3]], "color": [255, 0, 0]}].

style.name: Style
style.description: Bar (the default for values), line (the default for points and series) or dots. Points and series cannot be drawn as bars.

color.name: Colour
color.description: Colour of the bars or line. Defaults to the text colour in the integration's options.

background_color.name: Background colour
background_color.description: Colour behind the graph. Defaults to black.

x_min.name: X minimum
x_min.description: x value at the left edge. Defaults to the smallest x. Not used for bars.

x_max.name: X maximum
x_max.description: x value at the right edge. Defaults to the largest x. Not used for bars.

y_min.name: Y minimum
y_min.description: y value at the bottom. Defaults to the smallest y. Bars always start at 0.

y_max.name: Y maximum
y_max.description: y value at the top. Defaults to the largest y. Points outside the range are drawn at its edge.

maximum.name: Maximum
maximum.description: Older name for Y maximum. Give only one of the two.

label.name: Label
label.description: Optional short text shown in a strip above the graph.

save_slot.name: Save slot
save_slot.description: Program slot on the matrix that the graph is stored in (1 to 10).

hide_loading.name: Hide loading
hide_loading.description: Set the panel's brightness to 0 while the picture is sent, then put it back, so the panel's own loading animation is not seen.

live.name: Live
live.description: Show the picture straight away as a live frame instead of saving it in a slot (like the app's camera mode). save slot and hide loading are not used.

display_random_pixels.name: Display random pixels
display_random_pixels.description: Fills the LED matrix with pixels or squares in bright random colours that change at each step of a looping animation.

steps.name: Steps
steps.description: Number of different random pictures in the animation (1 to 50).

duration.name: Step duration
duration.description: How long each picture is shown, in milliseconds (20 to 10000).

colors.name: Colours
colors.description: How many bright colours the pixels use (2 to 256, default 4), spread evenly round the colour wheel from a random start. Random pixels hardly compress, so fewer colours send faster. Through an ESPHome proxy, 10 steps on a 192 x 32 panel take about 11 s with 2 colours, 20 s with 4 and 41 s with 16.

block_size.name: Block size
block_size.description: Size of each random-colour square in pixels (1 to 32). 1 colours every pixel separately, 2 uses 2 x 2 squares, and so on. Bigger blocks also make a smaller animation that sends faster.

save_slot.name: Save slot
save_slot.description: Program slot on the matrix that the animation is stored in (1 to 10).

hide_loading.name: Hide loading
hide_loading.description: Set the panel's brightness to 0 while the picture is sent, then put it back, so the panel's own loading animation is not seen.

draw_pixels.name: Draw pixels
draw_pixels.description: Colours single pixels on the LED matrix live, using its drawing mode. Much less data than a picture, so it shows almost at once.

points.name: Points
points.description: Pixels to colour as [x, y] pairs, for example [[0, 0], [5, 3]]. x runs 0 to width - 1 from the left, y 0 to height - 1 from the top.

rectangles.name: Rectangles
rectangles.description: Filled rectangles to colour as [x1, y1, x2, y2] corners (both included), for example [[0, 30, 95, 31]] for a bar along the bottom.

color.name: Colour
color.description: Colour of the pixels. Black [0, 0, 0] turns them off. Defaults to the text colour in the integration's options.

clear.name: Clear first
clear.description: Clear the whole panel before drawing. Off draws over what is already shown.

draw_frame.name: Draw frame
draw_frame.description: Paints several coloured layers of rectangles, pixels and text into one picture and sends it in one go, so the panel changes from the old picture to the new one at once.

layers.name: Layers
layers.description: Up to 32 layers, painted in order. Each has color [R, G, B] and any of rectangles ([x1, y1, x2, y2] corners, both included), points ([x, y] pairs), and text with x, y, size and anchor (l/m/r then a/m/s, for example rm).

background_color.name: Background colour
background_color.description: Colour behind the layers. Defaults to black.

save_slot.name: Save slot
save_slot.description: Slot 1 to 10 the picture is saved to. Defaults to the save slot in the integration's options.

hide_loading.name: Hide loading screen
hide_loading.description: Keep the old picture showing while the new one is sent, instead of the panel's loading screen.

live.name: Live
live.description: Send it as a live frame instead of saving it to a slot.

show_clock.name: Show clock
show_clock.description: Sets the matrix's time from Home Assistant and switches it to its built-in clock.

show_date.name: Show date
show_date.description: Show the date as well as the time.

countdown.name: Countdown
countdown.description: Runs the matrix's built-in countdown timer. Needs firmware that has the countdown (iPixel Color 3.8 and later offer it).

command.name: Command
command.description: Start a new countdown, pause it, resume it, or reset it to 0:00.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: Minutes to count down from, 0 to 90. Used by Start; Pause and Resume send the time too, as the app does.

seconds.name: Seconds
seconds.description: Seconds to count down from, 0 to 59.

stopwatch.name: Stopwatch
stopwatch.description: Runs the matrix's built-in stopwatch. Needs firmware that has the stopwatch (iPixel Color 3.8 and later offer it).

command.name: Command
command.description: Start the stopwatch from zero, pause it, resume it, or reset it.

set_schedule.name: Set schedule
set_schedule.description: Stores a daily on/off time on the matrix itself, so the display switches on or off at that time even when Home Assistant is offline. Also sets the matrix clock. When only some days are picked it also shows the clock, because that is the only way to give the matrix the date.

days.name: Days
days.description: Days the entry applies to. Leave empty for every day.

display_on.name: Display on
display_on.description: On turns the display on at that time, off turns it off.

number.name: Entry number
number.description: Which stored entry to write, 0 to 255. Sending the same number again replaces that entry.

rhythm.name: Music bars
rhythm.description: Draws the music visualiser's bars at the heights you give. The bars show for a second or two, so send it repeatedly (for example from an audio sensor) to keep them up.

levels.name: Levels
levels.description: Up to 11 bar heights, 0 to 15, left to right. Missing bars are 0.

rhythm_animation.name: Music animation
rhythm_animation.description: Runs the matrix's own music animation for a second or two; send it repeatedly to keep it running.

scoreboard.name: Scoreboard
scoreboard.description: Shows two scores on the matrix's built-in scoreboard. Send it again with new numbers to update the scores.

delete_slots.name: Delete slots
delete_slots.description: Deletes the messages or pictures saved in the given slots on the matrix.

delete_all.name: Delete all
delete_all.description: Deletes every message and picture saved on the matrix.

play_slots.name: Play slots
play_slots.description: Plays the messages or pictures saved in the given slots, one after another. Slots left out are hidden, not deleted: list them again to bring them back.

slots.name: Slots
slots.description: Slot numbers to play, 1 to 10. Give one slot to show just that one.

image_source.message: Give either a file or a URL for the picture, not both.

invalid_image.message: The picture could not be prepared: {error}

file_not_allowed.message: Home Assistant is not allowed to read {file}. Put the picture in /config/www or a folder listed in allowlist_external_dirs.

device_not_found.message: The LED matrix {address} is not in Bluetooth range.

not_seen_by_adapter.message: The Bluetooth adapter or proxy {adapter} cannot currently see the LED matrix {address}. Check the proxy is online, or set Connect via to Automatic.

connect_failed.message: Could not connect to the LED matrix: {error}

write_failed.message: Sending to the LED matrix failed: {error}

not_an_ipixel.message: The device does not have the iPixel write characteristic (0xFA02).

no_space.message: The LED matrix does not have enough storage for this message.

rejected.message: The LED matrix rejected the message.

invalid_message.message: The message could not be prepared: {error}

no_graph_data.message: Give one of values, points or series.

no_message.message: There is no message to send again yet.
